A: icons.svg renders blank when opened directly: root <svg> has no viewBox and no self-preview <use> row (symbols only)
report metaphor is a generic document with two text lines, the least distinctive glyph of the six
alert triangle overshoot (x 2.3..21.7) is aggressive; at 48px alert reads a touch wider than its siblings
glyph vocabulary is close to stock (lucide-like); limited originality
B: report's 3-bar mini chart clumps into a smudge at 16px and is muddy at 24px on 1x displays; the DECISIONS file never addresses this known small-size failure mode
settings sliders break their own stated system: edges claimed aligned at x3.5/x20.5 but row 2 starts at 4.5 and row 3 ends at 19.5, and the 2.25px rail stubs read as floating noise at 16px
asset cube is scaled to 0.9 of the live area (3.9..20.1) and reads slightly smaller/lighter than its neighbours when the row is scanned
1.75px stroke renders thin at 16px, losing presence against the dark panel compared with the rest of the family's apparent weight

notes: Both are competent, well-verified systems with valid symbol sheets, unique ids, currentColor and honest DECISIONS files. The brief's core asks - 16px legibility and equal-weight family consistency - decide it: A's 2px stroke row reads crisp and even at 16px on both themes, and A caught and designed out the exact defect B shipped (chart bars merging at small sizes); B's 16px row is lighter and less even, with a clumping report interior, a slightly undersized cube and ragged slider rails that contradict B's own stated edge alignment. B wins smaller points (self-previewing sheet, aria-label, a useful 16px-in-context row) but loses on the glyphs themselves.
